exact_sections.locator: Practice Points 1.1.1.1–1.1.1.2 and 1.1.3.1–1.1.3.2; summary PDF pages 34 and 54–57
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports GFR and urine-albumin testing, repeat confirmation, prior GFR or albuminuria trends, imaging, history, and the minimum chronicity context without diagnosing CKD from one result.

exact_sections.heading: Evaluation of cause and kidney-function context
exact_sections.locator: Practice Point 1.1.4.1, Figure 8, Table 6, and Practice Point 1.2.1.1; summary PDF pages 34–35 and 61
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports careful medical, family, medicine, urinary, systemic, examination, urinalysis, ACR, electrolyte, and imaging context in clinician-led CKD evaluation.

exact_sections.heading: Evaluation of albuminuria
exact_sections.locator: Practice Points 1.3.1.1–1.3.1.3 and Table 16; summary PDF pages 39 and 75–76
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports ACR, PCR, urinalysis, quantitative confirmation, and interpretation factors including haematuria, menstruation, exercise, and infection.

exact_sections.heading: Monitoring GFR and albuminuria in CKD
exact_sections.locator: Practice Points 2.1.1–2.1.5; summary PDF pages 40 and 81–82
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports clinician-arranged GFR and albuminuria monitoring and evaluation of a greater-than-20-percent eGFR change or ACR doubling without mapping fixed legacy intervals.

exact_sections.heading: Polypharmacy and drug stewardship
exact_sections.locator: Practice Point 4.3.1 and Figure 46; summary PDF pages 50 and 135–137
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports periodic medication review, accurate medication lists, adherence, continued indication, interaction, monitoring, reconciliation, and nephrotoxic-medicine context without treatment changes or doses.

exact_sections.heading: Referral to specialist kidney care services
exact_sections.locator: Practice Point 5.1.1 and Figure 48; summary PDF pages 51 and 140–141
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports clinician-led referral documentation for qualified sustained GFR decline, significant albuminuria with haematuria, refractory hypertension, persistent potassium abnormalities, and other listed circumstances.

records.source_organisation: NHS England
records.document_title: Adult breathlessness pathway (pre-diagnosis): diagnostic pathway support tool

exact_sections.heading: Purpose of this support tool; Scope of the problem
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Defines chronic adult breathlessness as a primary-care presentation and limits the pathway to chronic rather than acute or subacute symptoms.

exact_sections.heading: Diagnostic pathway — clinical assessment and initial investigations
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Specifies history, physical examination, and clinician-selected initial investigations for chronic persistent breathlessness.

exact_sections.heading: Diagnostic pathway — red flags
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Lists chest pain, haemoptysis, cyanosis, inability to speak in sentences, confusion, unilateral leg swelling, stridor, rapid progression, and low oxygen saturation.

exact_sections.heading: Key points — initial presentation, examination, and investigations
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Specifies onset and associated history, functional impact, exposures, medication context, vital signs, respiratory effort, cardiac and chest examination, and selected investigations.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.7.1–1.7.5 — maintenance and review
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports recording ongoing acne or relapse context and a clinician-completed maintenance review; no treatment is generated.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.1.12–1.1.14

exact_sections.heading: Section 1.3 - stable chest-pain assessment and investigation context

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.3.10–1.3.13 — specialist assessment, reassessment, and information
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting completed foot protection assessment, vascular or biomechanical review, clinician-selected reassessment, information already provided, and an entered follow-up plan.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.4.1–1.4.10 — ongoing orthopaedic management
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports selected orthopaedic follow-up, stability review, weight-bearing, cast or fixation context, and return review for non-improving symptoms in specified fracture populations.

exact_sections.evidence_summary: Requires structured fracture documentation, image and report continuity, honest information, questions, treatment expectations, rehabilitation, mobilisation, weight-bearing, management-plan communication, and documentation.

exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports adult recurrent epigastric pain, heartburn, acid regurgitation, bloating, nausea or vomiting, associated precipitants, meal timing, and clinician-discussed lifestyle documentation.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.3.1–1.3.4 — referral guidance for endoscopy
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports immediate specialist referral for significant acute gastrointestinal bleeding, medicine-cause review, prior endoscopy review, and further assessment when new alarm signs are present.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.4.2–1.5.2 — H. pylori context and review
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports clinician-reviewed H. pylori testing context and annual review for people needing long-term dyspepsia management; medicine names and doses are not mapped.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.6.1–1.6.16 and 1.11.1 — GORD management and specialist referral
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports clinician-documented reflux management, medication-plan discussion, review, and specialist referral where symptoms do not respond or remain unexplained; no dose or autonomous treatment text is mapped.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.1.1-1.1.8 - training, device maintenance, measurement technique, and postural assessment
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports validated and maintained devices, standardized measurement conditions, appropriate cuff size, pulse review, and clinician-recorded postural measurements.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.2.1-1.2.13 - clinic, ambulatory, and home blood-pressure assessment
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting repeated clinic readings, ABPM or HBPM source and averages, result context, annual measurement in relevant diabetes care, and clinician review without automatically diagnosing hypertension.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.3.1-1.3.3 - cardiovascular risk and target-organ assessment
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports clinician-led cardiovascular-risk discussion and review of urine, blood, retinal, and ECG assessments where actually performed or already ordered.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.4.15-1.4.24 - monitoring and annual review
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports clinic, home, or ambulatory blood-pressure monitoring, symptoms, medication and lifestyle discussion, and an annual review without generating targets, treatment, or advice.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.5.1-1.5.3 - severe hypertension and same-day specialist review features
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting measured severe blood pressure plus assessed retinal, neurological, chest-pain, heart-failure, kidney-injury, or phaeochromocytoma features as prompts, never as automatic conclusions.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.1.5–1.1.8 — postural hypotension symptoms and standing blood pressure
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting postural dizziness or falls context, lying or seated and standing blood pressure measurements, timing, symptoms, and clinician review without diagnosing orthostatic hypotension or changing treatment.

exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports at least 6 months of abdominal pain or discomfort, bloating, bowel-habit change, relation to defaecation or stool frequency or form, straining, urgency, incomplete evacuation, food association, mucus, and selected extra-intestinal symptoms.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendation 1.1.1.2 — red-flag assessment
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Requires clinical assessment and examination for suspected-cancer features and inflammatory markers for inflammatory bowel disease, with referral when present; specific cancer-feature fields require their own exact source.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.1.2.1–1.1.2.2 — diagnostic tests
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports full blood count, ESR or plasma viscosity, CRP, and coeliac antibodies in people meeting IBS criteria and identifies tests not required solely to confirm IBS.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.2.1.1–1.2.1.8 — dietary and lifestyle advice
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports clinician-documented lifestyle, activity, diet, symptom-trigger, and specialist dietary discussion; specific advice is not inserted automatically.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendation 1.2.5.1 — follow-up
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports agreed symptom-response-based follow-up, annual review, and investigation or referral when new red-flag symptoms emerge.

exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports orthopaedic review for new or worsening pain, limp, or loss of function related to a joint replacement while noting the absence of a general fixed monitoring schedule.

exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting missed doses, stopping or restarting, intentional or practical barriers, and support preferences without generating an intervention.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.3.1–1.3.2 — periodic review

exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting current prescribed, over-the-counter and complementary medicines, changes, discrepancies, discharge information, reconciliation and patient or carer involvement at care transitions.

exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports clinician-led review of benefits, harms, treatment burden, personal priorities, and a documented discussion about reducing or stopping treatment without generating a medication change.

exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports review of fever, cough, sputum, breathlessness, chest pain, fatigue or functional recovery, worsening or non-improving symptoms, systemic illness, and clinician-documented safety advice, with adult and child qualifiers preserved.

exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports reassessment when symptoms or signs do not improve or worsen, clinician-led referral, microbiology where specified, and CRP or procalcitonin review in the qualified hospital treatment-failure context.

exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports no routine post-inpatient follow-up radiograph, consideration at 6 weeks for smoking, age over 50, persistent or deteriorating symptoms, or unexplained weight loss, and shared decision-making using recent imaging, comorbidity, frailty, prognosis, treatment options, and preferences.

exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting an already prescribed treatment, adherence discussion, adverse effects, and clinician review of response; no medicine or dose is generated.

It does not assert cancer or generate referral.

exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports emergency transfer or escalation for high-risk presentations and documented monitoring, warning signs, and how to seek care for lower-risk presentations.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.8 and 1.11 — source identification and investigations

exact_sections.heading: Summary and pathology/radiology recommendations — traceable review and responsibility
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports a traceable record of review, action, responsibility, referral and handover for pathology and radiology results.

exact_sections.heading: Operational guidance — result review, patient communication, record and follow-up action
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting the specific test, reviewed result or report, communication and clinician-determined follow-up action.

records.source_organisation: Royal College of Anaesthetists
records.document_title: Guidelines for the Provision of Anaesthesia Services for Day Surgery 2025

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.12 and 1.17 — suitability and preoperative day-of-surgery assessment
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports clinician-documented day-surgery suitability, referral, VTE or pregnancy context, and preoperative checks.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.18–1.27 — recovery, discharge, information, and follow-up
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports pain scoring, unplanned admission, discharge protocol, written information, contact arrangements, escort or support, and discharge summary documentation.

records.source_organisation: Royal College of Anaesthetists
records.document_title: Guidelines for the Provision of Anaesthesia Services: Chapter 2 — Guidelines for the Provision of Anaesthesia Services for the Perioperative Care of Elective and Urgent Care Patients 2025

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 2.1–2.2 — assessment and specialist review
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports assessment before anesthesia or sedation and clinician review of concerns, results, risk, and shared decisions.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 3.6 and 4.1–4.4 — previous records and risk domains
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports previous anesthesia records and alerts plus age, comorbidity, medicines, allergy, surgery, pain, cognition, frailty, nutrition, lifestyle, psychological, functional, and chronic-pain risk assessment.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 4.2 and 4.6 — high-risk documentation and local policies
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documented high-risk review and local policies for tests, blood, fasting, medicines, escalation, referral, and pregnancy without generating an action.

records.source_organisation: World Health Organization and International Committee of the Red Cross
records.document_title: Basic emergency care: approach to the acutely ill and injured

exact_sections.heading: SAMPLE history and emergency disposition
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports signs and symptoms, allergies, medicines, past history, last intake, events or mechanism, examination, interventions, reassessment, and disposition documentation.

exact_sections.heading: Trauma secondary survey
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports inspection for wounds, bruising, swelling, tenderness, deformity, range of movement, neurological findings, severe pain, and other injury signs.

exact_sections.heading: Extremity trauma and perfusion
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports deformity, distal pulse, capillary refill, sensation, neurovascular compromise, open fracture, splinting, and perfusion reassessment documentation.

exact_sections.heading: Open wound and laceration assessment
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports laceration or abrasion, location, size and depth, bleeding, contamination, foreign-body concern, underlying structures, distal perfusion, dressing, splinting, tetanus, and return or disposition documentation.
